messages.subject: Binomial under preferential sampling?
parts:
Hello INLA Group!

This may be a naive question, but, is it reasonable to apply the preferential sampling approach, as described in the SPDE manual,  to a binomial (presence/absence) response?  That is, is there any reason why fitting a binomial point pattern and its associated marks jointly wouldn't be an effective strategy to deal with preferential sampling?  For example, using family = c("binomial", "binomial") or family = c("gaussian", "binomial") where both the first and second vectors consist of zeros and ones with a SPDE spatial effect on the first vector and using the "copy" feature to share the field with the second vector that also includes marks/covariates.  I've only seen examples with preferential sampling applied to a lgcp or Poisson likelihood.

Thanks,
John

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Binomial under preferential sampling?
parts:
Hi,

the preferential sampling model by Diggle et al, is a LGCP model where
the log intentsity is also observed with a non-preferential samples.
from this the gaussian/poisson is derived. yes, you can come up with
other forms for preferential sampling (the Diggle.et.al is not the only
one), and derive the model properties from there.


H
